subject: Quantum tunnelling
hook: QUANTUM TUNNELLING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Quantum tunnelling is not just a microscopic curiosity; scientists have demonstrated that it can occur on a macroscopic scale involving many particles behaving in unison.
angle_support: In 2025, John Clarke, John M. Martinis and Michel H. Devoret received the Nobel Prize in physics for experiments done in 1984 and 1985 that demonstrated how quantum tunnelling can be observed on a macroscopic scale, involving many particles.

In this experiment, they showed that they could control and investigate a phenomenon in which all the charged particles in the superconductor behave in unison, as if they are a single particle that fills the entire circuit.
title: Macroscopic Quantum Tunnelling: Whole Superconductors Tunnel Together
description: Scientists have shown that quantum tunnelling isn’t limited to tiny particles. A Nobel‑winning experiment demonstrated an entire superconducting condensate tunnelling as one across a thin barrier, revealing quantum behavior on a scale we can see.
narration: QUANTUM TUNNELLING IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You think tunnelling only happens to single electrons or atoms, a quirky quantum trick you see in labs. In reality, researchers have watched whole clouds of Cooper pairs tunnel together, acting like one giant particle across a macroscopic barrier. The effect spans a circuit visible to the naked eye, not just a nanometer‑scale curiosity. In 2025 John Clarke, John M. Martinis and Michel H. Devoret earned the Nobel Prize for a circuit that let an entire superconducting electron condensate tunnel at once. They placed two superconductors on either side of a 10 nm insulating barrier and cooled the device below one kelvin. The Cooper‑pair wavefunction extended across the gap, so every pair moved together, producing a single, quantized supercurrent that could be switched on and off—direct evidence of macroscopic tunnelling. It proves quantum rules can dominate visible systems, blurring the line between microscopic weirdness and everyday reality today.
